per_test_verdicts.root_cause_hypothesis: The hosting side is likely serving a page shell that renders locale buttons client-side but does not include the SEO head metadata in the initial HTML response. This can happen if the app is deployed as a client-side SPA without SSR/SSG, if the head tags were not configured in the app build, or if an edge/CDN rewrite is returning an index.html template that lacks the <link rel="alternate" hreflang> entries. As a result, crawlers/tests inspecting the document head see no link elements even though the UI shows language options.
per_test_verdicts.recommended_fix_target: Add the missing hreflang alternate link tags in the server-rendered <head> for all locales (en, es, pt), e.g. <link rel="alternate" hreflang="en" href="..." />, and make sure the hosting/deployment pipeline serves the fully rendered HTML rather than a client-only shell. If the site is built with a SPA framework, move SEO/head generation to SSR/SSG or use a head manager that injects links during server render. Also verify the locale URLs and canonical/alternate mappings are included in the deployed build and not removed by a CDN/edge transform or build optimization.
